title.narrative: INVESTING IN NUTRITION & EARLY YEARS PHASE 2 PROGRAM

description.narrative: The development objective of the Second Phase of Investing in Nutrition and Early Years Program-for-Results (PforR) Project is to enhance the delivery of services to accelerate the reduction of stunting in Indonesia. The PforR deepens the flagship partnership of the Government of Indonesia (GoI) and the World Bank to support stunting reduction under the ongoing first phase of investing in nutrition and early years program (INEY). The PforR modality is the GoI's preferred financing instrument and will streamline World Bank financing toward the stunting reduction program alongside ongoing health sector reforms. The new PforR will: (a) provide risk mitigation measures to the challenges of multisectoral coordination and the management challenges that constrain effective delivery of programs and interventions; (b) maintain focus on a core package of priority services critical to stunting reduction and early years development; and (c) generate data across the results chain and levels of government, including outputs and intermediate outcomes at the national, district, and village levels.
To enhance the delivery of services to accelerate the reduction of stunting in Indonesia.

condition.narrative: Not later than December 31, 2025, or such other date agreed with the Bank, the Borrower shall, in conjunction with the Bank, carryout a mid-term review of the Program (“Mid-term Review”), covering the progress achieved in the implementation of the Program.

Section I.A.1 of the Legal Agreement: The Borrower shall establish within three (3) months of the Effective Date, and maintain, atall times during the implementation of the Program, the following entities, all with staff, functions, and resources satisfactorytothe Bank: (a) a Steering Committee; (b) Implementation Committee.

Section I.A.2 of the Legal Agreement: The Borrower shall, at all times during the implementation of the Program, cause Bappenas tobe responsible for the overall coordination, planning, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of the Program activities, and theBorrower shall take or cause to be taken, all actions, including the provision of funding, personnel and other resources to enableBappenas to perform its respective functions under the Program.

Section I.A.3 of the Legal Agreement: The Borrower shall, at all times during the implementation of the Program, cause Bappenas andthe MOF to enable the Program implementation through ensuring that plans and budget allocations are consistent with the Program'stargets and policies as set out by the Steering Committee Team.

The Borrower shall establish within three (3) months of the Effective Date, and maintain, at all times during the implementation ofthe Program, the following entities: (a) a Steering Committee; (b) Implementation Committee; (c) Coordinating Project ManagementUnit (“CPMU”) within the Bappenas, which shall be responsible for the day to day coordination and implementation of the Projectactivities, (e) Project Implementation Units (“PIUs”), to be established in each of SOVP, Bappenas, MOH, MOHA, MOV, and BKKBN.

The Recipient shall ensure that the collection, use and processing (including transfers to third parties) of any Personal Datacollected under this Project shall be done in accordance with applicable national law and good international practice, ensuringlegitimate, appropriate, and proportionate treatment of such data.

title.narrative: Number of children under five receiving Pentavalent vaccine/DPT 1 (Number) in priority districts

comment.narrative: Number of children aged 0-60 months receiving Pentavalen (DPT â€“ HB â€“ Hib) vaccine in identified under-performing districts. The Pentavalent vaccine, also known as DPT-HB-Hib, is a combination vaccine that protects against multiple diseases, including diphtheria, pertussis (whooping cough), tetanus, hepatitis B, and Haemophilus influenzae type b. The Pentavalent vaccine is typically administered to infants as part of routine immunization schedules to provide early protection against these diseases. The indicator uses as the baseline the children in the 144 districts with coverage of first dose Pentavalent vaccine less than 92% in 2022.

title.narrative: Number of active Posyandu delivering essential health and nutrition services according to agreed standards

comment.narrative:
Definition of active Posyandu as stated in MOH Strategic Planning (MOH, 2019): 1. Conducting routine integrated health posts activities (providing healthcare services for pregnant women, infants, adolescents, productive age individuals, and the elderly) once a month, with a minimum of 8 times per year. 2. Providing minimum healthcare services for pregnant women, infants, and adolescents. 3. Having a minimum of 5 kaders
In this protocol, the definition of achievement of active Posyandu will be based on the above criteria with additional criteria of Posyandu reporting monthly activities to Pustu/Puskesmas.

title.narrative: Number of Puskesmas in priority districts that meet minimum clinical standards for service-readiness for essential maternal, newborn, child, and adolescent health and nutrition services

comment.narrative: The "Number of Puskesmas in Priority Districts that meet minimum clinical standards for service-readiness for essential maternal, newborn, child, and adolescent health and nutrition services, meeting requirements set forth in the Verification Protocol" refers to the count of Puskesmas located in Priority Districts that successfully fulfill the minimum clinical standards for service-readiness in providing essential health and nutrition services for maternal, newborn, child, and adolescent populations. This indicator aims to support efforts designed to improve the quality of essential healthcare and nutrition services for women (particularly pregnant mothers), newborns, children, and adolescents by addressing key service readiness gaps. In this context, service readiness is defined as the services package delivered at Puskesmas level in accordance with the Integration of Primary Health Care Program regulation/guideline (Permenkes and ILP Guideline). The service package provided at Puskesmas level refers to the provision of equipment and human resources, as defined by the standards outlined in Permenkes (number 43 and its revisions), aimed at meeting the healthcare needs of the community. Priority districts defined as in the regulation by Bappenas (Minister of National Development Planning/ Head of National Development Planning Agency) Decree Number Kep. 101/M.Ppn/Hk/06/2022 Regarding Determination of Regency/City Locations for the Accelerated Stunting Reduction Intervention Integration Program Year 2023). This DLR reflects the level of readiness and capacity of Puskesmas facilities to provide comprehensive and quality care to the targeted populations. By meeting the minimum clinical standards as per the regulation, Puskesmas in Priority Districts demonstrate their commitment to delivering effective, evidence-based, and standardized healthcare services. This supports the goal of improving maternal, newborn, child, and adolescent health and nutrition outcomes in the Priority Districts and contributes to the overall strengthening of the healthcare system.

title.narrative: Percentage of pregnant women in the priority districts receiving the sixth ANC visit

comment.narrative: The number of women/pregnant women who completedANC services in normal pregnancies at least 6 times. As stated in the Integrated ANC guideline, the sixth ANC visit (namely as K6) is defined as the contact of pregnant women with health workers who have clinical/midwifery competence to obtain integrated and comprehensive ANCaccording to standards during their pregnancy at least 6 times during their pregnancy with a time distribution: 2 times in the first trimester (0-12 weeks), 1 time in the second trimester (>12 weeks - 24 weeks), and 3 times in the third trimester (>24 weeks until birth), where at least 2 times pregnant women must contact a doctor (1ime in the first trimester and 1 time in the third trimester).

title.narrative: Number of Posyandu where at least 1 Kaders have completed the new basic training modules for maternal health, child (<5) health, school-age/adolescent health

comment.narrative:
â€œNumber of Posyandus with at least one Kader completing a certification for the maternal health, under-five child health and nutrition, school age /adolescent modules of the new 25 basic skills for Posyandu Kader MOH will finalize and issue training modules on 25 basic skills for Posyandu kaderâ€ " refers to the count of Posyandus where one of its Kaders has successfully completed the competecies in posyandu management, maternal and breastfeeding competencies, under-five child health competencies, as well as school-age and adolescent competencies, in accordance with the new training module on the 25 basic skills for Posyandu kader.
The Ministry of Health will complete and issue a training module "25 Basic Skills for Posyandu Kaders and Standard Home Visits," referring to a training module focused on 25 basic skills and standard home visits for Posyandu kaders. The training module will be delivered to at least one Posyandu cadre in each priority district. Once the module is approved, the Ministry of Health will monitor the number of Posyandu units with at least one cadre who has completed competencies in Posyandu Management, maternal and breastfeeding competencies, infant and toddler competencies, and school-age and adolescent competencies.
The training module aims to equip Posyandu cadres with the knowledge and skills needed to perform their roles effectively. The 25 basic skills encompass various aspects of health services and may include topics such as nutritional status and growth measurement, monitoring, promotion, breastfeeding support, immunizatio, family planning, health promotion, and disease prevention. Standard home visits refer to a set of established guidelines or protocols followed by cadres when visiting households to provide health promotion. MOH will issue a training on 25 basic skills and standard home visits for Posyandu kader. Among the 25 basic skills, topics should include: a. Posyandu Management b. Maternal Health (ANC) c. Health and nutrition for under-five children (nutritional status and growth measurement, monitoring, as well as promotion, feeding practices, immunization demand creation, including for diarrheal disease); d. School age and adolescent health and nutrition (IFA supplementation promotion)
